beats: Cast rule (episodes/e01-moe/FACTS.md: an expert is not a topic specialist; never label one by subject): the receptionist plus eight doctors told apart only by face and hair, no specialty props; the film numbers the doors in code (#0-#255), never names a department.
Hook: if the router keeps picking the same few experts, the rest never learn anything: two doors with endless queues, six with cobwebs and bored doctors (line_moe_two_famous_doors).

Top-k is discontinuous: a tiny change in the input or the router weights flips the choice from one expert to another: a marble on a knife-edge ridge (line_moe_marble_ridge); a switch, not a dimmer (reuse line_switch_dimmer).

The training trick: pick normally going forward, and going backward simply ignore the experts that were not picked (their gradient is zero): only the doctors who saw the patient get a feedback letter (line_moe_feedback_slots).

Rich get richer: the early favourites get all the practice and get picked even more, most experts are never trained, and who wins depends on the starting values: watering only two plants (line_moe_watering_two; reuse line_wilted_plant, line_dice_hand for the starting roll).

Fix 1 (DeepSeek V1/V2): an auxiliary load-balance loss that grows when a few experts take every token: a marshal moves people out of the long queue (line_moe_queue_marshal). The cost, in Zhongkai's words: like making everyone see the dentist even when some need an eye doctor; drawn without specialties as a patient sent past her first-choice doctor to one who is keen but unsure (line_moe_wrong_doctor).

Fix 2 (DeepSeek-V3, auxiliary-loss-free balancing): a bias per expert that is used only to choose, never to weigh the answers, nudged during training from the recent traffic (line_moe_peg_board) and frozen at inference (line_moe_padlock laid over the board).
Result: every expert gets work and learns something different (line_moe_all_doors_busy).
Takeaway + cliffhanger: balance is not only a training problem; when serving, it decides how many GPUs sit idle (tease L14-03).
Cover (line_cover_l14_02; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): two doors with endless queues, six shut doors with cobwebs and bored doctors.

drawings.name: line_moe_two_famous_doors
drawings.prompt: A long hospital corridor wall with a straight row of eight plain consulting-room doors, each with a small blank rectangular plate and a round handle, seen from the front. The first two doors on the left stand open with a doctor in each doorway, and in front of them two very long queues of patients snake back and forth across the floor, patients holding small blank tickets, some sighing, some checking their watches. The other six doors are shut, with cobwebs in the upper corners of their frames; in front of three of them a doctor in a white coat sits on a chair, bored: one dozing with the head tipped back, one yawning, one twirling a pencil. At the far right the receptionist (a cheerful young woman with her hair in a high round bun, small round glasses, and a plain short-sleeved tunic with a pen clipped to the breast pocket) sits at a small desk and points every new patient towards the two busy doors. Landscape image 1536x1024; the scene fills about 94% of the width and 80% of the height. No signs, no posters, no cross symbols, no writing on anything. No text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no logos anywhere.
